title: Edmund and the Bakery
premise: Dominic Okonkwo's struggling café is saved when a local literacy program assigns him an anonymous pen pal — who turns out to be Edmund Ashford, the bank's junior loan officer threatening to seize his building, and neither knows the other's identity at first. As their letters deepen into love, Dominic discovers Edmund has been quietly burying evidence that the bank's regional director fabricated Dominic's default to flip the property for a developer. When identities are revealed mid-festival, Dominic must choose between exposing Edmund's complicity or trusting the man who risks his career to make it right. They end the festival together, café saved and Edmund testifying, having forgiven themselves first.
about_author: August Galloway is the pen name of a former small-town journalist who spent a decade covering courthouse corruption before turning to romance. They write love stories where tenderness and accountability are the same act, and they still bake bread every Sunday.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. He counts the café's remaining days while kneading dough at 4 a.m., refusing his sister's loan offer out of pride. Emotional beat: weary defiance — a man who believes second chances are for luckier people.

chapters.title: The Letter in Slot Nine
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A community literacy program assigns anonymous pen pals; his first letter arrives with handwriting so elegant it feels like mockery. He writes back sharp and funny anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity cracking his armor.

chapters.title: The Man from the Bank
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Junior loan officer Edmund Ashford delivers the default notice to Okonkwo's Café, unnerved by Dominic's steady glare and the smell of cardamom. Emotional beat: professional duty colliding with a conscience he's learned to mute.

chapters.title: Ink and Irony
chapters.summary: Alternating letters, both POVs. Pen pals trade confessions — Dominic's father's lost bakery, Edmund's suffocating family expectations — each believing the other is a stranger. Emotional beat: intimacy blooming in the safety of anonymity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Hides
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Reconciling accounts, Edmund finds Dominic's payments were rerouted and marked late — someone inside the bank altered the ledger. Emotional beat: the first crack in his loyalty to the institution that made him.

chapters.title: The Developer's Dinner
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Regional director Vivian Marsh wines and dines a developer eyeing Dominic's block; Edmund realizes the default is manufactured. He says nothing. Emotional beat: complicity settling on him like ash.

chapters.title: Flour on His Cuffs
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Edmund returns — ostensibly to 'review the file' — and stays to help when the oven breaks. Banter turns warm. Emotional beat: Dominic hating how much he likes the enemy.

chapters.title: The Confession I Couldn't Mail
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund drafts a letter to his pen pal admitting what the bank has done, then burns it. Emotional beat: terror of being known and losing the one honest thing he has.

chapters.title: Festival Preparations
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Harvest Festival could save the café; Dominic signs up for the baking competition while Edmund, now a fixture, helps build the stall. Emotional beat: fragile hope, and a town beginning to root for them.

chapters.title: Slot Nine, Revealed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The program's reveal event pairs pen pals publicly — Dominic and Edmund, face to face, letters in hand. Betrayal detonates: the enemy was the confessor all along. Emotional beat: heartbreak and fury in front of the whole town.

chapters.title: Cold Ovens
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic tears up Edmund's letters and throws him out; his sister points out he's punishing Edmund for sins he himself hides — pride, silence, a father he never forgave. Emotional beat: the mirror moment.

chapters.title: Vivian's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Marsh offers Edmund a promotion to make him silent, dangling the career he sacrificed everything for. He accepts — then immediately hates himself. Emotional beat: corruption's seduction, and its cost.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Alone with his father's old recipe book, Dominic admits he's spent years punishing himself for the family bakery's failure. He rereads one letter — the burnt confession's ash still in Edmund's wastebasket memory. Emotional beat: beginning of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Copy in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund retrieves his backup of the falsified ledger from a locked drawer, hands shaking. Emotional beat: deciding that truth is worth more than the self he built.

chapters.title: Baking at Midnight
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic practices the competition entry — his father's lost recipe — and finds Edmund waiting outside in the rain with the ledger copies. Not forgiveness, but a hearing. Emotional beat: guarded thaw.

chapters.title: Loyalty on Trial
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund confronts Marsh privately; she threatens to destroy him and pin the fraud on a 'rogue junior officer' — Dominic. Edmund must choose whose loyalty he owes. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the café's last night before default, Dominic and Edmund bake together in silence, then talk until dawn — about fathers, failures, forgiveness. Emotional beat: love reassembled from honesty, still unspoken.

chapters.title: Festival Day
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The baking competition; Dominic wins with his father's recipe as the town cheers. Then Marsh arrives with eviction papers, timed for maximum humiliation. Emotional beat: triumph ambushed.

chapters.title: Edmund Stands Up
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Before the crowd, Edmund publicly presents the falsified ledger, resigns, and names Marsh. Justice outside the law — the town as witness. Emotional beat: ruin and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Ash
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Marsh is suspended pending investigation; the bank freezes the default. Dominic must decide whether Edmund's sacrifice buys trust or only proves he hid the truth for months. Emotional beat: love weighed against betrayal.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Unemployed, Edmund writes Dominic one final letter through Slot Nine — no anonymity left, everything at stake — and reads it aloud at the café door. Emotional beat: naked vulnerability, the mirror finally faced.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Bakery
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Dominic answers by handing Edmund an apron. The café reopens with a new sign; the festival's last lanterns rise over a town that chose its own. Emotional beat: forgiveness completed — of each other, and of themselves.
